Subject: RE: RE: Realtime inference — abnormal latency + 5xxs this morning

Triage update (short):
- Observed state: prod-us dedicated GPU pool at 92% utilization across nodes; queued token backlog increased by ~60% in the last 45m. KV-cache hit rate for FastLedger's model dropped from 84% -> 46% due to an evictions spike.
- Root cause hypothesis: a recently scheduled "indexing/embedding refresh" job (customer-side background batch) is running heavy long-sequence requests during their peak, causing cache thrash and raising effective per-request compute. The cluster is still within "reserved" limits by booking, but headroom is effectively consumed leading to queueing -> p95 blowup and occasional model OOMs returning 5xx.

Immediate mitigations we can take (recommended order):
1) Throttle or reschedule FastLedger's background job (ask customer to pause) — fastest drop in contention.
2) Flip route to the quantized model variant for checkout route (quantized has ~10-15% lower accuracy on edge cases but reduces per-token GPU time).
3) Enable tightened prefix caching and extend TTL for FastLedger's common prefixes (will improve KV hit rate).
4) If approved, authorize burst nodes (2 x g5x) for 3 hours to restore headroom while we implement cache fixes; requires exec sign-off due to cost/commit.

I'll attach the kvcache dump + trace markers to the internal ticket. If we cannot get the background job paused in 15-20m, recommend authorizing burst capacity now.

Attachments: redwood-kvcache-dump.txt
JIRA: https://app.redwood.ai/ops/alerts/ALRT-1123

-David
David Kim
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Elaine — thanks for the quick data. Short summary and plan: 

What we saw:
- p95 increased to ~2.6s, 5xx rate ~3.2%, effective reserved throughput drop ~22%.
- Internal observation: KV-cache hit rate dropped significantly; dedicated GPU pool at ~92% utilization; likely contention from a background batch job you recently scheduled.

Immediate plan (next 3 hours):
1) Can you pause the background indexing/embedding refresh job for the next 30–60 minutes? That single action historically restores KV hit rate quickly and reduces queueing.
2) If pausing is not possible, we will: a) flip the checkout route to the quantized model variant (opt-in, expect ~15% perf delta) and b) enable expanded prefix caching on your route.
3) We've recommended a short burst (2 x g5x for ~3 hours) to buy headroom while we stabilize — this requires exec sign-off from Redwood; I have cc'd Vivek for authorization.

Customer impact & SLA: if the burst is declined and we fail to meet throughput SLOs, we should be prepared to discuss proportional SLA remediation. I'm flagging this for leadership given the potential breach.

Morning / next steps on our side:
- David's infra team will be on a conference bridge to watch headroom and apply cache/route changes once you confirm.
- Marissa will coordinate a short bridge for your ops and our on-call.

Can you confirm whether you can pause the background job now? If so, we'll watch for improvements and avoid burst costs. If not, please confirm and we'll move to the fallback path.
